previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 25%), left ventricular thrombus, chronic kidney disease, diabetes, and prior AAA repair was admitted for evaluation of bright red blood per rectum. He had a therapeutic INR of 4.0 prior to admission, and labs showed a drop in hematocrit from baseline (41.5% to 31.6%) over 24 hours, though he remained hemodynamically stable. CT abdomen showed a mild caliber change at the splenic flexure, but no acute pathology. Colonoscopy and EGD revealed no active bleeding source, though blood was present in the cecum. Capsule endoscopy identified a slow bleed from a mucosal lesion in the distal jejunum. Given the stability of his hemoglobin and the high risk of thromboembolism from his known LV thrombus, anticoagulation was resumed with warfarin, bridged by heparin. His beta-blocker and diuretic were temporarily held but restarted as his condition stabilized. He was discharged home on warfarin, with a bowel regimen, and scheduled for outpatient double balloon enteroscopy to treat the bleeding site.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo man with cardiomyopathy (EF 25%) who presented with chest 
pressure and dyspnea and concern for altered mental status in 
ED.  
.  
#) Dyspnea: The patient was at his baseline by the time that he 
had reached the medical floor from the ED, after having received 
60 mg IV Lasix there. This was likely a mild CHF flare with 
superimposed acute viral bronchitis (the patient had upper 
airway sounds on exam.) His home Lasix was increased from 
alternating doses of 40 mg and 20 mg every other day to 40 mg 
daily. Of note, the patient has multiple admissions for SOB with 
a similar course- near resolution by the time the patient has 
arrived on the floor. The patient would benefit from outpatient 
cardiology management- perhaps in outpatient ___ clinic with 
Dr. ___- to prevent multiple hospitalizations for these mild 
symptoms. 
.
Of note, as above, the patient did have upper airway sounds on 
exam, but without leukocytosis, fever or productive cough. 
Therefore, this was likely a viral bronchitis and the patient 
was not treated with antibiotics.
.
Of note, he has ICD for primary prophylaxis in nonischemic 
cardiomyopathy with LVEF < 30%.  It was placed for inducible VT 
on EP study.  On Amiodarone was started in ___ for prevention 
of sustained VT which occured in ___ with failed ATP therapy by 
ICD and leading to ICD Shock.
.
#) Chest pressure: Patient presented with 10 hours of chest 
pressure, that had recurred over the past few days. There was 
low concern for ACS given this history. EKG did not show signs 
of ischemia and he had two sets of negative enzymes. His chest 
pressure resolved throughout admission. Continue home 
metoprolol, ASA, niacin, statin; patient no longer on ACE 
secondary to ___.
.
Of note, the patient might benefit from hydralazine/long-acting 
nitrate given that he is not on an ACE-I. This was not started 
inpatient because the patient did not have room in his BP to 
tolerate it, but this could be considered as an outpatient.  
.
#) Ventricular bigeminy: Pt had bigeminy on telemetry during 
admission but remaiend hemodyamically stable. Patient has pacer 
and ICD in place.
.
#) Altered Mental Status: On the floor he had had waxing and 
waning mental status- occasionally forgeting the year or place. 
What is more marked is that he has jerking/twitching movements 
during his sleep with talking and lip smacking. We spoke to his 
ex-wife, with whom he is currently living, who explained that 
these sleeping behaviors have been increasing over the past few 
weeks, with more confusion during the day. In addition, he lies 
in bed all day long (which has been going on for at least a 
year) and she has found him crying recently. 
 
We noted that his med recc here states he is on 62.5 mg daily 
imipramine but we confirmed with both his ex-wife and pharmacist 
that he has been taking 125 mg daily. In addition, the patient 
has not seen his psychiatrist in ___ years, although the 
psychiatrist has adjusted his med doses slightly over the phone. 
We consulted psychiatry about this discrepancy and his AMS. 
Psychiatry was concerned that he may have tardive dyskinesia and 
AMS from too high of an imipramine dose, and recommended a 
complete taper off. They also recommended that the patient stop 
imipramime and perphenazine completely (given their risks for 
mental status changes in the elderly) and switch medications to 
different anti-psychotics. The patient seemed amenable to this. 
He will initially folllowup with his prior Psychiatrist so that 
he can have quick followup but will consider transitioning to a 
BI Psychiatrist for convenience. He will also be set up for 
neuropsychiatric testing as an outpatient.  
.
He was discharged on an Imipramine taper to end at 50 mg daily; 
his Psychiatrist and PCP can further adjust this and facilitate 
a change in psychiatric medications.
.
#) Back Pain: Patient was initially described as having flank 
pain, and had a CT abdomen/pelvis in the ED. However, history 
and exam revealed that this was not in fact flank pain but 
instead lower back pain. This was likely musculoskeletal and was 
treated inpatient with Tylenol. 
.
#) CKD: Slight elevation on admission, likely due to poor 
forward flow in the setting of mild CHF exacerbation. At 
baseline on discharge.
.
#) LV thrombus: INR subtherapeutic at 1.8 here and so coumadin 
was increased to 5 mg daily. He will continue to follow INRs at 
___ ___.
.  
#) Depression/paranoia: Continued perphenazine with imipramine 
taper; see discussion above.   
.  
#) HTN: Continued metoprolol, amiodarone 
.
#) Type II DM: Continued glipizide. 
.
#) Hx GI bleed: Stable HCT here. Outpatient F/U already 
scheduled. Per Dr. ___ will need repeat capsule. 
.
#) AAA with ulcer on imaging: Seen in past hospitalization, 
patient was supposed to followup with Vascular surgery as an 
outpatient but does not appear to have ___ this. Will set up 
outpatient followup.

radiology_notes.text:
PA AND LATERAL CHEST, ___ AT 1140 HOURS

HISTORY:  Left flank pain and shortness of breath.

COMPARISON:  Multiple priors, the most recent dated ___.

FINDINGS:  Lung volumes are markedly diminished.  There is relative
accentuation of the pulmonary vasculature, particularly to the upper lobes
consistent with cephalization and prominence of interstitial markings, likely
indicating volume overload.  An indwelling single chamber AICD is in stable
and standard course and position from a left subclavian approach.  Aortic
tortuosity is again noted and stable.  Likewise, the cardiac silhouette
remains borderline enlarged, but stable.  No definite effusion or pneumothorax
is noted.  The osseous structures are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  Mild diffuse interstitial edema, likely cardiogenic in etiology. 
Repeat radiography after appropriate diuresis recommended to assess for
underlying infection.

INDICATION:  ___ man with LV thrombus and acute delirium. Evaluate for
intracranial process.

COMPARISON:  CT of the head from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT images were acquired through the head without contrast.  Bone
kernel reconstructions and multiplanar reformations were obtained and
reviewed.  Images are degraded due to motion.  Repeat images also degraded due
to motion.

FINDINGS:

No acute hemorrhage, large vascular territory infarct, shift of midline
structures or mass effect is present.  The ventricles and sulci are normal in
size and configuration.  The visible paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells
are well aerated.

IMPRESSION:

Motion degraded images but no acute intracranial process.

INDICATION:  ___ man with left flank pain, evaluate for stone or other
acute abdominal process.

COMPARISON:  Abdomen and pelvis CT from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT images were acquired through the abdomen and pelvis with IV
contrast.  Multiplanar reformations were obtained and reviewed.

The partially imaged lungs show mild bibasilar atelectasis.  The partially
imaged heart shows a right-sided pacemaker.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST:

The liver, spleen, both adrenals, both kidneys, pancreas and gallbladder are
unremarkable.  There is a small amount of calcification in the right pleura.

No abdominal, retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy by CT size
criteria is present.  No abdominal free fluid or free air is present.  The
small and large bowel loops are unremarkable.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:

The rectum, sigmoid colon, bladder, prostate, and seminal vesicles are
unremarkable.  No pelvic free fluid, pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy by CT
size criteria is present.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:

The visible osseous structures show old rib fractures of the left eleventh,
tenth and ninth ribs.  No suspicious lytic or blastic lesions are present.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No renal stones or acute intra-abdominal process.

2.  Calcification of the right pleura.

3.  Healed rib fractures on the left.

REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Followup of the patient with mild congestive heart
failure after diuresis.

PA and lateral upright chest radiographs were reviewed in comparison to ___ study.

Current radiograph demonstrates still presence of mild interstitial pulmonary
edema.  There is slightly more focal opacity in the right mid lung that
potentially may represent asymmetric part of edema or an infectious process. 
Continued evaluation of the patient after continuous diuresis is suggested.

Otherwise, no significant change since the prior study has been demonstrated.
